summary: A crowded step throws away a quarter less: the sound the fight asks for is a record off a pool now
Every line of interface type is measured, and the nine that could not be read can be now
Milestone 9 closed: the palette's shapes are measured from the renderer, and two bodies borrow the ship's own silhouette on purpose
The menu behind the glass: a panel now puts the page underneath it to bed instead of the title shining through
MARKS: a dark centre punched through what can hurt you, a lit one in what you want - a second signature over the palette, measured
The menu announces itself: the title's song starts as the page opens, wherever the browser allows it
Key rebinding: a CONTROLS rack inside the settings, thirteen keys you can move, and no page left printing an old one
Gamepad support: left stick flies, right stick aims and fires, a shoulder dashes, A launches and Start holds the run
Touch support: a thumb flies the ship with a stick that appears where it lands, one button dashes, and the gun aims and fires itself for a run flown on a finger
A writing pass over every line the game says: one kill is 1 KILL, one clock wording everywhere, and the three voices held apart by a test
First-run tutorial: three prompts in play that teach flying, firing and dashing, and vanish once the run proves it knows them
Daily run: one arena a day, seeded by the date, with a best of its own
A step throws away four to seven times less: it was Math.hypot listing its arguments on the heap, 38 ways a step
The menu has a song of its own, and a step throws away a third of what it used to
The deal asks the gun: three primaries were being dealt cards they could not spend
The two slow primaries are priced in bodies now: the weapon ladder reads PASS at 1.13x
Two fixes to what a run takes with it, and three rules turned into checks
F3 puts up the developer's panel: frame cost, arena counts, and pool usage
The soundtrack gets a tune, a floor, and eight bars of harmony instead of four
VACUUM: every 10,000 points the arena empties itself into the ship
ATTRACTOR: a card that buys how far off the loot is yours
AUTO-FIRE and AUTO-AIM: the game can be flown with the keyboard alone
O opens the settings: shake, flash, score numbers, particles, and the mixer
The card a run ends on says what ended it: what took the last hull, and what every hull before it went to
Esc or P holds the run and shows its stats and its build; G gives the run up
The title writes its own name, and then keeps moving
The hangar keeps a third rack: all thirty awards, lit when they are yours and priced when they are not
The codex keeps a rack of the last twenty runs: seed, ship, clock, score, and whether they cleared
Awards: thirty-one on the back of the hangar, won in the run, said on the glass the moment they turn true
The codex: C opens what this save has met, and runs fill it in as they end
Four perks, five ranks each, and both racks fitted to the window
Four of the five ships cost stardust now, and the hangar is where you buy them
Stardust every run pays, and the hangar you spend it from
One versioned save document, and the settings that live in it
Two volume sliders and a mute that outranks them, with a readout that says what a key did
The music plays the run: drums at 2:00, a boss tempo, and a heartbeat at one hull
UI ticks, hits pitched by the body's size, and loot that climbs as it comes in
Noise everywhere: explosions rumble, the dash whooshes, and a hit pulls the music behind a wall
Generated music: a 110 BPM sequencer with pad, bass and arpeggio, on its own bus under the fight
Endless keeps climbing past every ceiling the schedule spent, and ends when the crowd outlasts the gun
Endless: the win hands the arena back; the room only shakes when it is worth it; the last card cannot be clicked away
The run can be won: a second ending, the hush, and the card that says ARENA CLEARED
The Eclipse's shell walks its door: a gap that travels, shown the whole of the way
The Eclipse's last phase lifts an arm: fans of blades shown whole, then swept
The darkness covers the whole window now, and a test measures that it does
The Eclipse's darkness: the room goes dark and what is left is what is shining
The Eclipse: a dark sun at 15:00 that drags you in and bursts out in shells
The Hive's last phase: it comes apart into three smaller hives and one hull bar stays one fight
The Hive: a mass of cells that breeds swarms and can be shot apart
The Warden calls Darters out of its own hoop: phase 3 is a summon and the Warden is finished
The Warden's second beat: a ring of shots with a door in it, thrown between the spokes
Bosses: the arena shuts a room round the duel, and the Warden walks in at five minutes
Ships: five hulls to fly, each one the gun it was built around
Swarm: the fifth primary - slow micro-missiles that each find a body of their own and go off in it
Lance: the fourth primary - a line of light down the whole arena, after a moment of winding up
The run's own build, down the left edge: a mark for every upgrade taken and a pip for every rank
Thermal shock: a corpse that wore both fire and frost takes the room with it, and the first synergy the deck can deal
Reroll and banish: the deal can be argued with twice a run
Turret: a gun is set down across the road ahead of you and holds that ground for ten seconds, aiming and firing at whatever it can see
Tether: a dash ties a line of light from where it started to wherever you get to, and everything standing on it burns
Mines: the ship drops mines out of the way it was going, and a body that walks into the ring on the floor pays for the road
Magnetar: the shards you pick up charge the field round the ship, and when it is full it lets go
Afterimage: the dash leaves images of the ship standing where it was, and the bodies next to them chase those for two seconds
Overcharge: stand still for a second and the next pull of the trigger is worth double
Leech: every body you bring down is worth a hull back, and the first card in the game that gives something
Chill: every hit the ship lands takes the speed out of them, and a cold body coming apart throws ice
Burn: every hit the ship lands sets the crowd alight, and a body that dies alight passes it on
The agent bridge: the game playable by a coding agent over stdin/stdout
The sniper: a stationary eye that draws a laser across the whole arena, and the last body of the roster
Survival check: the median is in the tool, and the firepower milestone closes on it
Arc: the third primary - lightning that finds the nearest body and leaps four of them
Scatter: six pellets in a 30-degree cone at half the pulse's reach, and the title screen asks which gun you fly
Nova: a ring of damage leaves the ship every 8 s, and a rank buys one more inside the cycle
Orbitals: a ring of drones round the ship, two more per rank, biting whatever stands in it
Ricochet: a shot that would die turns on to the next body, one more per rank
Pierce: one pull of the trigger goes through one more body per rank
Split shot: one pull of the trigger fires a fan of shots
The level-up choice: three cards, three upgrade lines, and a run that grows as it goes
The swarm: up to twenty small fast bodies that arrive as one wave member and fly as one thing
The shielder: it armour-plates the crowd around it, and the crowd goes cheap when it dies
Elites actually arrive now: one wave in five after 8:00 carries a gold body
Elite variants: gold bodies with four times the hull, a large shard, and a chance of a heal
The window edge points at the danger you cannot see
The bomber: a blast whose circle you are shown while it lives
Enemies arrive as waves, bought with a spawn budget that grows with the run
The spitter: a telegraphed enemy shot
The darter: a telegraphed lunging enemy
The sky is a nebula: drifting clouds baked once, painted behind the stars
Wreckage and a wake: three particle shapes on the pool
The arena is a world: 3000x3000, a camera that follows and leans, energy walls at its edge
Hit-stop: the run holds its breath on a big kill and on a hit
Pre-rendered glow sprites: no blurs, no per-frame gradients
The dash: 220 px on rails, a 2.5 s wait, invulnerable through it
The ship flies like the plan says: acceleration, braking, a 6 px hitbox
Fixed-step simulation, seeded runs, collision grid and pools: the foundations release
First playable: the single-file neon arena survival baseline
